title: Use fetch controller full timing info for navigation timing
body: Extract the full timing info from `navigationParams`'s fetch controller when creating and initializing a `Document` object for network navigations, and remove the duplicate call to "create the navigation timing entry". When `navigationParams`'s fetch controller is null (such as for `about:srcdoc` and `javascript:` URL documents), coarsen an unsafe timestamp captured at the start of the algorithm for `loadTimingInfo`'s navigation start time and create the `PerformanceNavigationTiming` entry from a fallback fetch timing info (with #13285 and #13287 tracking follow-ups for navigations supplied with a response and cross-origin isolated coarsening). Also pass `navigationParams`'s navigation timing type (fixing an unbound `navigationTimingType` variable), the response's cache state as `cacheMode`, and `0` for `criticalCHRestart`. Tests: https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/65457. Fixes #12887. - [x] At least two implementers are interested (and none opposed): * Chromium (already matches) * Gecko (already creates navigation timing entries for non-fetched documents) - [x] [Tests](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt) are written and can be reviewed and commented upon at: * https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/65457 - [x] [Implementation bugs](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#handling-pull-requests) are filed: * Chromium: already matching * Gecko: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2096497 * WebKit: https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=332813 - [x] Corresponding [HTML AAM](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/) & [ARIA in HTML](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/) issues & PRs: N/A - [x] [MDN issue](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#handling-pull-requests) is filed: N/A - [x] The top of this comment includes a [clear commit message](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/COMMITTING.md) to use.
